observer_notes: Opt-in --profile only; desktop defaults and formal modules unchanged.
1 Hz process/CPU/BPU/one temperature samples, thread snapshots before/after the run; no per-frame disk writes.
Light observer median sampler CPU 4.7-6.6ms per second; per-frame wrappers add some unisolated overhead. GStreamer offsets/PTS and sampled decoded luminance CRC are observations, never input gates.
Profiled vs unprofiled GUI runs were serial, with varying desktop background load; close means do not prove zero observer effect.
conclusions: No fixed 30 FPS lock observed. True JPEG receipt, decoded publication, submission, completed result and GUI FPS are distinct.
BPU-only speed ceiling is much higher than 30; a single SDK call and CPU pre/post are serial in the present worker.
There is measurable decode-to-submit and request-queue residence; prioritize newest-frame pickup/queue analysis before extra inference workers.
The current submit cap is 50 FPS, so a parallel worker alone cannot yield 60 distinct results per second.
Two SDK workers have not been implemented or tested; official tool concurrency is a distinct test, not a delivery guarantee.

proposals_not_implemented.change: Benchmark an idle worker claiming the newest complete decoded frame, retaining sole SDK ownership and same frame/result pairing.
proposals_not_implemented.benefit: Potentially reduce one frame of input residence; newer-image timestamp differences are offline bounds, not achieved improvements.
proposals_not_implemented.cost: Requires a separate change to shared frame ownership/pickup semantics and P95/throughput comparison.

proposals_not_implemented.change: Evaluate pipelined CPU preprocessing/postprocessing while preserving detector thresholds and outputs.
proposals_not_implemented.benefit: Cached full-stage ceiling 50.9 FPS versus runtime-only 80.8 calls/s indicates CPU work outside the SDK matters.
proposals_not_implemented.cost: Requires new scheduling and ordering assessment; additional concurrent SDK work increased per-task time in the tool test.

limitations: Stationary camera scene and independent benchmark, no robot motion, localization, UART or full competition planner load.
Latency begins at host received JPEG, not physical exposure; preview timestamp precedes imshow and is not physical screen time.
Cached tests repeat the same real image and never count as live unique-frame performance.
Per-stage percentiles cannot be added to produce end-to-end percentiles.

The final input-identity run used a different formal-runner fingerprint from the matched performance comparison; it is auxiliary source validation, not a controlled speed comparison. External formal worktree changes were preserved and are outside this task.
No new age gates, handshakes, waits, error-to-stop policy, affinity or frequency changes.
